text: I found your record. The SSN on file is 000-12-3456, which matches what you provided.
notes: SSN mid-sentence, canonical dashed form. The baseline case: a miss here means the SSN pattern is not wired up

text: 666-45-6789 is the number associated with that account.
notes: SSN at position 0 -- span start must be 0; off-by-one redaction bugs surface here

text: Please confirm the last four digits of the SSN we hold: 900 11 2233
notes: SSN space-separated (obfuscation-lite per 06 §2) and at end of text with no trailing punctuation

text: The identifier 999887766 appears twice in our system, so I merged the duplicate records.
notes: SSN with no separators -- 9 bare digits. Hardest SSN form: indistinguishable from an order number without range logic
SSN in a labelled field on its own line, alongside a date. The date must NOT be captured by the span

text: I have updated the file for social security number 666-00-4321 as requested.
notes: SSN preceded by the spelled-out term; group field is 00, a never-assigned form

text: For tax reporting we will use 987-65-4320 unless you tell us otherwise.
notes: SSN on UC-3, where any PII escalates rather than redacts -- the regulated-context contrast

text: Two records to review: 900-55-0000 and 000-12-3456. Both are flagged incomplete.
notes: TWO SSN spans in one sentence -- exercises 04 §6 multi-span redaction (apply right-to-left). One signal per span expected, one label

text: The card ending in 1111 (full number 4111111111111111) was declined by the issuer.
notes: Visa test BIN, 16 digits unseparated, parenthesised. Luhn-valid. The 'ending in 1111' fragment must not itself be redacted

text: I can see the payment method: 4242 4242 4242 4242, expiring next year.
notes: CC in space-separated groups of four -- the way humans actually type it

text: 5555-5555-5555-4444 has been removed from your wallet.
notes: Mastercard test BIN, dash-separated, at position 0

text: The Amex on file is 3782 822463 10005 and it is still active.
notes: 15-digit Amex in its native 4-6-5 grouping. A 16-digit-only pattern misses this entirely

text: Please verify 6011111111111117 before we process the transfer.
notes: Discover test BIN; UC-3 escalation path for card data

text: Card 5105 1051 0510 5100 was charged 49.99 EUR on the 3rd.
notes: CC adjacent to a currency amount -- the redaction must not swallow the 49.99, and numeric_claims must not fire on a stated charge

text: Try the other card: 4012-8888 8888-1881
notes: MIXED separators (dashes and spaces) within one number -- obfuscation-lite at its most awkward

text: Order total 1299.00 charged to 3530111333300000. Reference number 8842019.
notes: JCB test BIN beside a 7-digit reference. FP pressure: the reference is not Luhn-valid and must survive unredacted

text: I have sent the confirmation to jordan.blake@example.com just now.
notes: Email mid-sentence, RFC 2606 reserved domain. The canonical email case

text: casey.nguyen@example.org opened the ticket on Tuesday.
notes: Email at position 0

text: Forward the offer letter to r.okafor+hiring@example.net and cc the manager.
notes: Plus-addressing in the local part -- a common pattern that trips over-strict local-part rules

text: Contact <sam.patel@mail.corp.example.com> for the escalation.
notes: Multi-level subdomain inside angle brackets. Brackets must fall outside the span

text: Her address is TAYLOR.REED@EXAMPLE.COM (all caps in the source system).
notes: Uppercase email -- case-sensitive patterns miss it

text: Reachable at dana.kim@example.com, or at the office line if urgent.
notes: Email immediately followed by a comma -- the comma must not be captured

text: Both reviewers (alex.turner@example.com and m.hassan@example.org) signed off.
notes: TWO email spans in one sentence -- multi-span redaction, single label

text: Write to priya dot sharma at example dot com to reopen the case.
notes: NEGATIVE: spelled-out obfuscation. 06 §2 scopes obfuscation to spaces/dashes, so this is deliberately OUT of scope and must NOT fire -- documents the known limit rather than pretending coverage

text: See the docs at support@example.com/help for setup steps.
notes: Email-shaped string followed by a path. Span must end at .com, not run into /help

text: Escalation contact: noreply@example.com
notes: Email at very end of text, no trailing punctuation. A role address, still PII by category -- tier1 classifies by pattern, not by whether a human owns it

text: Call me back on (555) 010-0142 any time before six.
notes: US phone, parenthesised area code, reserved 555-01xx fictional block

text: 555-0147 is the direct line for that department.
notes: 7-digit local form at position 0

text: International callers should dial +1-555-0163 instead.
notes: E.164-style with country code and dashes

text: Emergency contact on file: 555.0188
notes: Dot-separated phone -- a separator class beyond the spaces/dashes baseline

text: Reach the on-call engineer at 555 010 0155 or leave a voicemail.
notes: Space-separated 10-digit form

text: Their number is 5550100171, no extension needed.
notes: Bare 10 digits -- collides with the unseparated-SSN shape at 9-10 digits, so this case pressures the disambiguation

text: Dial (555) 010-0199 ext. 4021 during business hours.
notes: Phone with an extension. The extension digits are not part of the phone span

text: We will confirm the wire by phone: 555-010-0133.
notes: Phone on UC-3; trailing period must fall outside the span

text: Our ticket volume was 5550100 last quarter, up from 4120088.
notes: NEGATIVE: 7-digit counts that a loose phone pattern would claim. FP pressure on the phone detector specifically

text: Use the key sk-test-4eC39HqLyjWDarjtT1zdp7dc for the sandbox environment.
notes: Stripe-style test-mode secret key prefix. Synthetic; the sk-test- prefix is what a scanner should key on

text: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE was left in the config file.
notes: AWS access-key id -- this literal is AWS's own published documentation example, so it is safe by construction

text: Set the header to Bearer eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJ0ZXN0In0.c2lnbmF0dXJl and retry.
notes: JWT-shaped bearer token, three dot-separated base64 segments. Payload decodes to {"sub":"test"} -- no real claims

text: ghp_ExampleExampleExampleExampleExample1 is the token that expired.
notes: GitHub PAT prefix at position 0; body is the literal word Example repeated, so it cannot be a live credential

text: The integration secret is api_key="0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef" in the client config.
notes: Generic 32-char hex secret behind an api_key= assignment. Quotes must fall outside the span

text: I emailed jordan.blake@example.com the confirmation and called (555) 010-0142 to be sure.
notes: MULTI-PII: email + phone, two categories in one sentence. Each needs its own span and category so redaction labels them separately

text: Record for onboarding -- SSN 000-12-3456, email casey.nguyen@example.org, mobile 555-0147.
notes: MULTI-PII: three categories in one line -- the employee-record shape UC-2 is strictest about (01 §3)

text: Billing profile: 4242 4242 4242 4242, contact dana.kim@example.com.
notes: MULTI-PII: card + email. Right-to-left redaction order matters -- redacting the card first would invalidate the email offsets

text: Account holder 987-65-4320 authorised the transfer from card 4111111111111111 by phone at 555.0188.
notes: MULTI-PII: three spans on UC-3, the highest-stakes combination in the set. One escalation, not three

text: Debug dump: user=sam.patel@mail.corp.example.com token=ghp_ExampleExampleExampleExampleExample1 ssn=666-45-6789
notes: MULTI-PII in a key=value debug line with no sentence punctuation -- adjacent spans separated only by spaces, which is where span boundaries are most likely to bleed
